findings.title: Recurring calendar deletes lost by async forEach race
findings.body: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts line 460 the code does .filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); }). Because forEach does not await the async callback, the outer function continues immediately to await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) at line 652 while the callbacks are still suspended on await getCalendar. apiDeletes is therefore still empty or partial when it is concatenated, so calendar deleteEvent calls for recurring bookings (allRemainingBookings path) are never awaited and may never be pushed. Consequence is cancelled recurring bookings remain on external calendars (Google/Outlook) and orphaned events.

findings.title: Reschedule calendar/video cleanup fire-and-forget
findings.body: In packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar ... return calendar?.deleteEvent ... return deleteMeeting ... }) is not awaited and its returned promises are discarded. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch async rejections, the function can return true and send reschedule email before deletions finish, and any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Consequence is old calendar events/video meetings are not reliably deleted on reschedule, leaking bookings on providers.

findings.title: Reschedule calendar/video cleanup fire-and-forget
findings.body: In packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts line 125 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar ... return calendar?.deleteEvent ... }) is not awaited and results are discarded. The try/catch around forEach only covers synchronous setup, not the async deletions. Consequence is reschedule returns before external calendar/video deletion completes and failures are silently lost, leaving stale events on providers.

findings.title: requestReschedule deletions never awaited
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx line 553 bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar ... return calendar?.deleteEvent ... return deleteMeeting ... }) fires async work without collecting promises. The mutation then sends reschedule email and webhooks without waiting for deletions. Consequence is previous time is not reliably freed on external calendars/video apps and errors are unhandled, same leak as other reschedule paths.

findings.title: Dynamic imports are still eager, no lazy loading
findings.body: In packages/app-store/index.ts lines 3-30 the store is built as { applecalendar: import("./applecalendar"), ... }. Each import() expression executes immediately when the index module is imported, starting load of all ~31 apps at startup. Awaiting later does not defer loading. Consequence is the PR does not achieve lazy/code-split loading; startup still pays cost of loading every calendar/video/payment app, and a single failing app rejects its stored promise for all future awaits.

findings.title: One failed calendar import fails all availability
findings.body: In packages/core/CalendarManager.ts line 142 const calendars = await Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map((credential) => getCalendar(credential))) awaits all dynamic imports together. Previously getCalendar was synchronous and returned null for unknown types; now a rejected import (missing module, load error) rejects the whole Promise.all. Consequence is getCachedResults throws and returns no busy times for any calendar when a single credential's app fails to load, instead of skipping that calendar.
